identity.title: High Star Formation Rates in Turbulent Atomic-dominated Gas in the Interacting Galaxies IC 2163 and NGC 2207

paper_type_evidence.quote: We observed NGC 2207/IC 2163 in CO(1-0) with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA). The present paper is devoted to determining the spatially-resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt (cite: kennicutt12) relation in this galaxy pair.

evidence.quote: a distance $D = 35\pm2.5$ Mpc from the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED) for a Hubble constant of $H = 73$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ corrected for infall towards Virgo.

distance_source.value: NED, H = 73 km/s/Mpc corrected for Virgo infall

evidence.quote: a distance $D = 35\pm2.5$ Mpc from the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED) for a Hubble constant of $H = 73$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ corrected for infall towards Virgo.

question.value: How does the star formation rate surface density depend on atomic, molecular and total gas surface density at 2.4 kpc scales in the interacting pair IC 2163 and NGC 2207, and does it differ from other galaxies?

evidence.quote: We are interested in whether this relation on a scale of $2.4$ kpc diameter differs from that in other galaxies, and whether it is the same in both galaxies here.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00357.S.
IC 2163 and NGC 2207 were observed in 34 pointings using ALMA at the $^{12}$CO(1-0) frequency of 115.27 GHz ($\lambda$ 2.6 mm).
at the $^{12}$CO(1-0) frequency of 115.27 GHz
We made naturally weighted maps of CO emission with a point spread function of $2.00^{\prime\prime} \times 1.52^{\prime\prime}$ (HPBW), beam position angle $68.5^\circ$
The rms noise per channel is $3.7$ mJy beam$^{-1}$

provided.value: HI cube, 21 km/s channels, beam 13.5"x12", 6 hr on source, obtained 1990

evidence.quote: The HI is from VLA observations obtained in 1990 using a hybrid CnB array with an extended north arm

provided.value: 24 um images for SFR (MIPS 1 pBCD and HiRes deconvolution)

evidence.quote: were measured from the MIPS 1 pBCD image obtained from the Spitzer archive in 2013; the resolution is $6^{\prime\prime}$.
obtained by Deidre Hunter with the Lowell 1.1m telescope in 1999
who provided their HiRes 24 $\mu$m data to us as a FITS image
we use $X_{\rm CO}= 1.8 \pm 0.3 \times10^{20}$ H$_2$ cm$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$ from (cite: dame01)
we took inclinations of $i = 40^\circ$ for IC 2163 and $35^\circ$ for NGC 2207 (cite: elmegreen95b)
We made naturally weighted maps of CO emission

masking.value: mask from cube convolved to 6"x6"; unblanked if >2.5x rms (7.9 mJy/beam) in >=2 adjacent channels

evidence.quote: Regions were left unblanked if they exceeded 2.5 times this rms noise for at least 2 adjacent channels in an area of at least 1 arc sec.

primary_beam_correction.value: applied before making the 551x301 pixel x 64 channel subcube

evidence.quote: After correcting for primary beam attenuation, we made the $551\times301$ pixel $\times64$ channel subcube
For more details on the observing procedure, see (cite: kaufman16).

what.value: SFR calibration combining Halpha and 24 um

evidence.quote: was used to obtain the SFR, following (cite: kennicutt09)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA calibration, CASA version, arrays/configurations and observing dates
Imaging details (cell size, deconvolver, cleaning threshold)
Details of the CO data reduction, deferred to Kaufman et al. 2016
Exact aperture positions are tabulated, but the HI kinematic separation of the two galaxies is not described

method.value: Natural-weighted cube, blanking mask from 6" convolved cube, primary beam correction, subcube

evidence.quote: we made a blanking mask by convolving this cube to $6^{\prime\prime}\times6^{\prime\prime}$ HPBW, where the noise was 7.9 mJy/beam.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive H2 mass and surface density

method.value: Convert CO to H2 with XCO, deproject with inclinations

evidence.quote: To convert surface density to face-on, we took inclinations of $i = 40^\circ$ for IC 2163 and $35^\circ$ for NGC 2207 (cite: elmegreen95b).
The scale is 170 pc per arcsec.

validation.value: Discussed effect of different XCO and i

evidence.quote: We discuss the implications of different $X_{\rm CO}$ and $i$ in Section [4](#sfrcorrel).

method.value: SFR = 5.5e-42 (L[Halpha] + 0.031 L[24um]) in apertures 14" = 2.4 kpc, with extinction corrections

evidence.quote: We chose source apertures with a diameter of $14^{\prime\prime} = 2.4$ kpc.

key_parameters.value: 24 um aperture correction 1.61 for Feature i; Galactic A_V = 0.238 mag

evidence.quote: applied an aperture flux correction factor of 1.61 from the MIPS Instrument Handbook

validation.value: Repeated with all images convolved to 14"x14"; conclusions unchanged

evidence.quote: None of the conclusions of this paper were affected by this change.

method.value: Plot Sigma_SFR vs Sigma_HI, Sigma_H2 and total gas, and vs molecular ratio; compare with THINGS

evidence.quote: Figure [3](#fig:n2207_alma_ks1c) shows these correlations.
The total integrated CO line flux in the subcube is $S(CO)=505$ Jy km s$^{-1}$.
NGC 2207 has $M(H_2) = 2.3\times10^9\;M_\odot$ for a CO line flux of 265 Jy km s$^{-1}$.
$\Sigma_{\rm H2}/\Sigma_{\rm SFR}=50$ Myr

results_numeric.quantity: Mean HI velocity dispersion of 16 HI-dominated regions in NGC 2207

evidence.quote: The mean HI velocity dispersion for the 16 green circles in N2207 (Fig. [4](#fig:n2207_alma_ks3)) is 42 km s$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: HI-dominated high-SFR regions lie mostly in the outer NGC 2207; H2-dominated ones in the IC 2163 ocular ridge.

evidence.quote: The HI-rich regions of high $\Sigma_{\rm SFR}$ are on the periphery of the galaxy that underwent the retrograde, perpendicular encounter (NGC 2207)

claims.hypothesis: Do HI-dominated regions follow the normal molecular Kennicutt-Schmidt relation?
claims.experiment: Compare Sigma_SFR vs Sigma_H2 for 44 apertures with THINGS
claims.result: HI-dominated high-SFR regions lie high above the linear molecular relation (H2 consumption time ~300 Myr)
claims.finding: They have excess SFR relative to molecular gas but normal SFR relative to total gas (~1 Gyr)

evidence.quote: The HI-dominated gas at high SFR (green points) lies high off the linear molecular relation.

claims.hypothesis: Turbulence explains the atomic-dominated star-forming regions
claims.experiment: Compare locations with HI velocity dispersion
claims.result: Mean dispersion 42 km/s vs ~10 km/s in normal galaxies
claims.finding: Consistent with flattened density PDF from compressive high Mach number turbulence

evidence.quote: This is consistent with theoretical predictions of a flattening in the density probability distribution function for compressive, high Mach number turbulence.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Different XCO or inclination (including warp) do not remove the HI-rich peculiarity

evidence.quote: Inclination effects would not seem to be causing the peculiar HI either.

limitations_admitted.value: About 25% absolute SFR uncertainty from 24 um calibration

evidence.quote: The absolute calibration of the 24 $\mu$m term in the SFR leads to an uncertainty of about 25% in the absolute determination of the SFR

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 44 apertures, no formal fits or uncertainties on relations
Single XCO assumed; dark H2 in HI regions not constrained
Halpha NII contamination and extinction corrections uncertain
